solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Run off with single girlfriend? It's lawful

parts.note: to leg it is slang for running away
the Roman numeral I is one, a single
a mate is a partner or close companion

explanation.surface: Someone elopes with an unattached girlfriend and asks whether that is allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the slangy charade; 'with' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimate and lawful are synonyms, both meaning allowed by law.

clue.text: Appliance needing large unit of current?

parts.note: L is the clothing abbreviation for large
the amp is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: Asking whether a household device draws a big current.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp is an electrical device for giving light, a household appliance.

clue.text: Name oddly associated with elegant refined chap

indicators.note: refined suggests something worked over and remade, so these letters are reshaped
oddly takes the letters in odd positions of the word

explanation.surface: A suave, cultured man is associated with a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives NM from 'Name'; 'refined' reorders NM with ELEGANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman is a man, especially a courteous one; chap is informal for a man.

clue.text: Catches second character up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a part is a character played by an actor

explanation.surface: An actor in a secondary role is promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns S plus PART to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Traps catch animals, so as a verb traps means catches.

clue.text: No term's complicated for teachers

indicators.note: complicated means tangled up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word term's provides the letters TERMS

explanation.surface: Teachers find no school term straightforward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' rearranges NO plus TERMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mentors are trusted advisers who guide and instruct, a kind of teacher.

clue.text: Mariner acquires objectives

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
gets means acquires or obtains

explanation.surface: A sailor achieves his goals.
explanation.definitionFit: Targets are goals one aims for, the same as objectives.

clue.text: Slip looking both ways

indicators.note: a word looking both ways reads the same forwards and backwards, so the answer is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone slips while checking traffic in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is informal British slang for a blunder or slip-up.

clue.text: Declare over deal

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Someone announces a bargain is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls; 'deal' is softwood timber, typically pine.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, to declare a view.

clue.text: She lets bra loose getting excited

indicators.note: loose means let free, so these letters are set in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman lets her bra loosen and gets worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' links wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathless can mean panting with excitement or eager anticipation.

clue.text: Ray's male adult, thank you very much!

parts.note: a grown male is a man
ta is informal British thanks

explanation.surface: Someone called Ray has grown up into a man, and is thanked effusively.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Ray' is 'is', a link to the wordplay; TA is everyday British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A manta is a very large species of ray, a flat-bodied fish.

clue.text: A rotter's case in domestic tale

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces go inside the word for domestic

parts.note: domestic as opposed to foreign means native

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A scoundrel's lawsuit features in a story of home life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A rotter' looks like a villain, but only the rotter's case, its shell, is used; 'in' puts those pieces just after the first letter of the domestic word.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is a story or account, so a tale fits.

clue.text: Ace partner, pure at heart, in buff

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace
a mate is a partner

indicators.note: at heart takes the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: A partner of a top player is innocent at heart, and naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in buff' plays on 'in the buff', naked; 'in' is the link and buff is an enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A buff is a keen enthusiast, and an amateur is a non-professional enthusiast.

clue.text: Girl is someone, at heart, flexible

indicators.note: at heart says the answer sits in the middle of the words before it, running across them

explanation.surface: Deep down, a girl is a pliable sort of person.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissome describes a body that is supple and lithe, so flexible.

clue.text: Quick beer, right?

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Someone checks they can grab a fast beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alert means quick to notice and respond, sharp-witted.

clue.text: Juvenile teen's a clod, misbehaving

indicators.note: misbehaving means acting wildly, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: teen's supplies the letters TEENS

explanation.surface: A young teenager is an oaf who behaves badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A juvenile is a young person not yet adult, the same as a teenager.

clue.text: Cheeky impressions?

parts.note: reads like impudent impersonations, but means small hollows pressed into the cheeks

explanation.surface: Mischievous impersonations by a comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimples are small natural dents in the cheeks, literally impressions on the face.

clue.text: The French with less than clean clothes

parts.note: la is a French word for the
under means less than, below

explanation.surface: French people wear clothing that is not quite clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces; 'clean clothes' is a verb phrase, to wash them.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder is to wash and iron clothing.

clue.text: One reproduces a design made by awkward clients

indicators.note: awkward clients are difficult ones, so these letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A designer's work is produced by fussy customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made by' is a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut-out sheet through which a pattern is painted repeatedly.

clue.text: Force swindle on mark without resistance

parts.note: a con is a swindle

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the mark goes round the letter

parts.note: a stain is a mark
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Pressure a con artist into a deal, marking him down without a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking; 'on' joins CON to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to compel or oblige, which is to force.

clue.text: Lethargy of Liberal facing sound of wrath

indicators.note: sound of says we want a word that is pronounced like the word for wrath

parts.note: wrath is anger

explanation.surface: A political Liberal's listlessness stands up against an angry noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' puts L in front. ANGUOR is said like ANGER, at least in non-rhotic British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Languor is a pleasant tiredness or inertia, close to lethargy.

clue.text: It's correct if you look inside

definitions.text: It's correct if you look inside

indicators.note: look inside says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to examine something closely to make it right.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'It's' cannot stand for the answer; the whole clue defines it (to correct), so it is an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: To rectify is to put right, to set something straight.

clue.text: Glows seen around opening of religious tombs

indicators.note: around says the word for glows wraps round the other letter

parts.note: something that glows shines

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Lights gleam around the doorway of a religious burial site.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrine can be a tomb of a saint or a revered person, a holy burial place.

clue.text: Devout following catching Queen

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: since means following or after
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a common abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A pious fan of royalty who has caught a glimpse of the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A devout person is earnest and genuine in faith, so sincere.

clue.text: Thus cover is given for stable

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A lid is fitted to keep something steady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is given for' links wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid means firm and steady, not likely to give way, hence stable.

clue.text: Revolt rising for social outcast

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to revolt is to disgust or repel

explanation.surface: An uprising for a person rejected by society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolt' looks like a noun for a rebellion, but it is the verb meaning disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: A leper, figuratively, is someone shunned by others, a social outcast.

clue.text: In this we're together — and on stage!

definitions.text: In this we're together — and on stage!

parts.words: In this we're together — and on stage!
parts.note: acting in this means acting together, and it is also a live musical performance

explanation.surface: A rallying cry that everyone is united, even as performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In concert' means jointly; a concert is also a show on a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A concert is a public musical performance, and acting in concert means acting in agreement.

clue.text: Quits from business, never to return

indicators.note: to return says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words following

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone abandons trade, vowing never to come back.
explanation.definitionFit: To be quits is to be even, owing nothing to each other.

clue.text: Spot missing outside of the ear

indicators.note: missing outside means losing the first and last letters

parts.note: to spot something is to notice it

explanation.surface: A blemish missed on the outer part of the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' is the verb, NOTICE, which loses N and E, its outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the medical adjective for relating to the ear.

clue.text: Understanding former wife, saucy one's sweetheart

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
pert means cheeky or saucy
one's is read as one is, I and IS, giving IS
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: Grasping that an ex-wife was a cheeky person's darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is a crossword convention: the heart (middle letter) of 'sweet'. 'one's' reads as I + S.
explanation.definitionFit: Expertise is skilled knowledge, a thorough understanding of a subject.

clue.text: More than close squeeze?

definitions.meaning: something better than roughly right is precise, spot on
to squeeze money from someone is to extort it, demand it

explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precisely correct, and as a verb means to demand or extort payment.

clue.text: Tense annoyance creates fatigue

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
ire is anger or annoyance

explanation.surface: Stress and irritation wear a person out.
explanation.definitionFit: To fatigue someone is to weary or exhaust them, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Why person ice-skating circles very fast?

indicators.note: the clue words circle, or enclose, the answer running through them

explanation.surface: Asking why a figure skater goes round in circles at great speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circles' looks like a description of the skating but tells you the answer lies within 'Why person ice'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypersonic means travelling at over five times the speed of sound, extremely rapid.
